skill.name: firmware-analyst
skill.description: Guides authorized firmware extraction, reverse engineering, emulation, and security assessment for embedded and IoT devices.
skill.summary: Guides authorized firmware analysis from acquisition through vulnerability reporting.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms high-risk dual-use guidance around raw device extraction, privileged chroot emulation, private key discovery, and command injection payloads. Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives caused by code fences, and no prompt injection attempt was found. The skill should remain limited to authorized firmware security work with stronger safeguards around privileged commands and exploit payloads.

remediation.issue: Privileged emulation commands use sudo and chroot with untrusted firmware contents.
remediation.suggestion: Require an isolated virtual machine or disposable lab host before any privileged emulation, and prefer least-privilege containers where possible.

remediation.issue: Raw device extraction reads /dev/mtd0 and stores the image in /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization checks and store firmware dumps in a restricted working directory with controlled permissions.

remediation.issue: Command injection examples include system reconnaissance and /etc/passwd access payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Replace dangerous payloads with benign lab-only markers and state that testing must occur only on authorized targets.

remediation.issue: Private key and credential discovery guidance lacks evidence handling rules.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions to redact secrets, restrict access to findings, and coordinate disclosure with the device owner.

remediation.issue: Firmware download example uses an unauthenticated HTTP URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS examples and require checksum or signature verification before analyzing downloaded firmware.

content.value_statement: Firmware reviews can miss hidden services, weak credentials, and unsafe update paths. This skill guides authorized extraction, analysis, emulation, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides firmware acquisition through vendor downloads, UART, JTAG, SPI, and flash extraction methods.
Recommends firmware tools such as binwalk, strings, checksec, Ghidra, QEMU, and Firmadyne.
Organizes analysis into identification, extraction, filesystem review, binary review, emulation, and reporting.
Lists common firmware vulnerability classes, including hardcoded credentials, command injection, memory corruption, and information disclosure.
Provides an assessment checklist and report outline for authorized firmware security reviews.
limitations: Does not include runnable automation scripts or parsing libraries.
Assumes the user has legal authorization and suitable lab hardware.
May require privileged system commands and specialized tools outside the skill.
Does not replace expert reverse engineering judgment or coordinated disclosure planning.

use_cases.title: Review Router Firmware
use_cases.description: Plan extraction, filesystem triage, and reporting for an authorized router security assessment.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Hardening
use_cases.description: Check firmware images for exposed credentials, weak services, unsafe update mechanisms, and debug interfaces.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Findings
use_cases.description: Turn firmware analysis notes into clear findings with impact, evidence, and remediation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Firmware Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized firmware image.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have authorization to assess this firmware image. Help me plan the identification, extraction, analysis, and reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Extracted Filesystem
prompt_templates.prompt: I extracted a firmware filesystem. Help me prioritize checks for credentials, services, web interfaces, permissions, and update security.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Binary and Service Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis of binaries and exposed services.
prompt_templates.prompt: I found several firmware binaries and network services. Help me assess architecture, hardening, risky interfaces, and likely attack paths.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Emulation and Report Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for lab emulation and final documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a safe lab emulation plan and convert the results into a security report with remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: I have a vendor firmware image and permission to test it.
output_examples.output: A phased assessment plan covering image identification, extraction, filesystem review, binary triage, emulation options, and report structure.

output_examples.input: The extracted filesystem contains web scripts, startup files, and suspicious credentials.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review checklist that separates immediate credential handling, web interface analysis, service exposure, and remediation evidence.

output_examples.input: I need to explain firmware findings to an engineering team.
output_examples.output: A concise findings outline with impact, affected components, reproduction boundaries, and practical remediation steps.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, device ownership, and testing scope before analyzing firmware or hardware interfaces.
Use an isolated lab system when running untrusted firmware tools, emulators, or extracted binaries.
Record firmware hashes, tool versions, commands, assumptions, and evidence handling steps.
anti_patterns: Running untrusted firmware or extracted binaries with sudo on a production workstation.
Publishing credentials, private keys, or device-specific secrets found during analysis.
Testing exploit payloads against devices or services without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What kind of firmware work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports authorized extraction planning, static analysis, emulation planning, vulnerability triage, and security reporting.

faq.question: Does it run firmware analysis tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and checklists. Users must run tools in their own authorized lab environment.

faq.question: Can it help with hardware extraction methods?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common UART, JTAG, SPI flash, NAND, NOR, and chip-off acquisition concepts.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: No. Firmware testing should use isolated lab systems, copied images, and clearly approved targets.

faq.question: How should discovered secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Treat them as sensitive evidence. Limit access, avoid public disclosure, and coordinate remediation with the owner.

faq.question: What tools does the skill mention?
faq.answer: It references binwalk, strings, checksec, Ghidra, QEMU, Firmadyne, and several filesystem extraction tools.
